items.title: $SMCI Shorts want you to think export-control trouble is unique to Supermicro, but it's been routine in tech for decades. Microsoft paid
items.content_excerpt: $SMCI Shorts want you to think export-control trouble is unique to Supermicro, but it's been routine in tech for decades. Microsoft paid $3.3M in BIS/OFAC penalties in 2023 for 1,339 violations tied to Russia, Cuba, Iran and Syria. Apple settled with OFAC in 2019 over App Store dealings with a sanctioned party. In 1999 the Power Mac G4 was so powerful it fell under US supercomputer export rules, restricting sales to dozens of countries. The charges here target individuals, not the company, and Supermicro is cooperating with US and Taiwan authorities. Export control has always chased cutting-edge tech, and AI servers are just the newest front. This is a compliance fight, not a broken business. https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy1394

There's also a longer-term argument that delayed PC upgrades represent deferred demand rather than permanently lost sales. But first I want to see how INTC behaves when the market opens Monday.

items.content_excerpt: $CORZ Leased customer power capacity was 1,120 MW at Sep 30 in the 10-Q, billable capacity was 485 MW. Leased means committed under contract whether service has started or not, billable means service has started and the company is actually billing. CoreWeave was about 590 MW of that leased total with 485 MW billing. The other roughly 530 MW is the July AMD and Neocloud leases, and none of that had commenced at period end.

Diluted EPS was 0.47 dollars vs basic EPS of 3.42 dollars. items.content_excerpt: $VIR To put a pin on the buyout talk. Here's why I am not in favor now. Multi-Pillar Valuation Story - If Vir sells out now, we will only get paid for Hepatitis Delta. Platform Multiples: Retaining independence allows us to capture the compounding upside the masked TCE oncology platform validates further. Selling out prematurely risks handing a multi-platform oncology engine over to Big Pharma at a single-asset price. Revisit after ECLIPSE-2 and ECLIPSE-3.

items.title: $FIGR so to the bear who is saying SNDK is trading at 6x PE and FIGR is trading at 24x Let me educate you For SNDK The market gives it a low
items.content_excerpt: $FIGR so to the bear who is saying SNDK is trading at 6x PE and FIGR is trading at 24x Let me educate you For SNDK The market gives it a low P/E because it expects those peak earnings to fall when the cycle turns. There's an old chip-investing saying: buy memory stocks at a high P/E and sell at a low P/E, because a low P/E often marks the top. - FIGRs 24x reflects growth. Earnings went from about $15M to $87M a quarter in a year, and investors pay more for that So SanDisk's 6–8x isn't "cheap" and FIGR's 24x isn't "expensive." They're priced for different futures - So about $6–10. That would only happen if the market believed FIGR's earnings were about to collapse, as if the same fear that was applied for memory chips. But for a profitable company growing like FIGR, that's an extreme bear scenario, not a reasonable fair-value comparison

items.content_excerpt: Investors were also reacting to the latest nonfarm payrolls report, which came in much better than expected at an increase of 165,000 in October. That was well above the 59,000 that economists polled by Dow Jones had anticipated. The unemployment rate also moved down to 4.1%. Economists had expected it to hold steady at 4.2%. All three major averages posted losses on the week, even after Wednesday’s big rally in the wake of the election. The Nasdaq lost 3.4% and the S&P 500 dropped 2.7%. The 30-stock Dow was the outperformer, sliding 0.9%. Looking at the history of Nasdaq corrections shows tech stocks often find their footing over the next three-to-six months, but trading can remain rocky in the near term. $VOO

$SMCI Shorts want you to think export-control trouble is unique to Supermicro, but it's been routine in tech for decades. Microsoft paid $3.3M in BIS/OFAC penalties in 2023 for 1,339 violations tied to Russia, Cuba, Iran and Syria. Apple settled with OFAC in 2019 over App Store dealings with a sanctioned party. In 1999 the Power Mac G4 was so powerful it fell under US supercomputer export rules, restricting sales to dozens of countries. The charges here target individuals, not the company, and Supermicro is cooperating with US and Taiwan authorities. Export control has always chased cutting-edge tech, and AI servers are just the newest front. This is a compliance fight, not a broken business. https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy1394
